question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=-\frac{x}{4},$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-\frac{1}{4}\,⟹\,-4\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $0$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $-1$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}5{e}^{-x/4}\,\text{d}x & =5{\int }_{0}^{4}{e}^{-x/4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{\int }_{0}^{-1}{e}^{u}\cdot (-4)\,\text{d}u \\  & =-20{\int }_{0}^{-1}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-20\cdot {e}^{u}\,{|}_{0}^{-1} \\  & =-20({e}^{-1}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =-20({e}^{-1}-1) \\  & =20-20{e}^{-1}\end{aligned}
$$
